#1964. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1963. Andriy Shevchenko demands apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk over ‘baseless’ failed drugs test claims

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk said.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t said it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’

Asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk said: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko said in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism

‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’

#1962. Arsenal lock down defence as Hincapie joins Rice and Raya in contract talks

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:53

Arsenal are in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a new contract, according to the BBC, despite the defender having more than four years left on his current deal. The Ecuador international, 24, is the third key player to be tied down in a single week after Declan Rice and David Raya. BBC football correspondent Sami Mokbel says he is set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms even if he is strongly linked to Barcelona in the last weeks.

On Monday evening, Sky Sports News reported that Rice, 27, had verbally agreed a new deal with Arsenal. On Tuesday morning, Sky Sports, citing The Athletic, reported in its live coverage that goalkeeper Raya, 31, had also agreed a new long-term contract. His current deal runs to 2028, and the Spaniard has won the last three Premier League Golden Gloves, according to Sky. The report came shortly after Raya admitted he would one day like to play in La Liga.

Arsenal have not officially announced any of the agreements, but the BBC says the club are preparing to confirm new contracts for Rice, Raya and Jurrien Timber. Riccardo Calafiori, 24, is also next in line, according to the BBC. The Italian left-back, who joined from Bologna in 2024, has a contract until the summer of 2029, and the club want to begin talks with him in the not-too-distant future.

Hincapie joined on 1 September 2025 from Bayer Leverkusen on a season-long loan with an option. The BBC reported at the time that Arsenal had agreed a £45m fee for a permanent deal, and saw the Ecuadorian as a direct replacement for Jakub Kiwior, who left on loan for Porto. Boss Mikel Arteta introduced him on the club website, saying: ‘Piero is physically really impressive, and his versatility and tactical flexibility give us strong options in defence.’

On 25 June 2026, the club announced they had exercised the option and the move became permanent from 1 July, without disclosing the fee. According to Arsenal, Hincapie made 39 appearances in all competitions in the title-winning season, was the club’s player of the month in February and April, and scored his only goal in February at Wolverhampton Wanderers. The defence he slotted into conceded the fewest Premier League goals for the third season running, according to the club.

The BBC now gives 47 appearances for Arsenal in total, which suggests he has added eight this season. One of them was the November game in Prague, where Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1.

The Hincapie deal is not a protection against losing him for free, as that risk does not exist with more than four years remaining. A one-year extension on better terms looks mostly a reward and a way of aligning his wages with the role he has in the squad. He has gone within a year from a loan replacement for Kiwior to a player the BBC lists among the key members of Arteta’s squad.

The common thread in all three cases is timing. Rice had 18 months plus an option left, according to Sky, Raya had a deal to 2028 and Hincapie more than four years. Arsenal are not negotiating under pressure from expiring contracts, which sends a clear signal that, after the title, they want to build on the existing core. In Raya’s case there is also a defensive logic, as the goalkeeper himself opened the subject of Spain and a new contract makes such temptations more expensive. If Timber is added, and Calafiori in the coming months, Arteta will have a goalkeeper, three defenders and the driving force of midfield all on new contracts.

#1959. 'It's a LIE': Bullish Morgan Rogers hits back at claims Cole Palmer isn't committed to England as Three Lions star appears to suggest Thomas Tuchel is 'wrong' for questioning Chelsea team-mate

Published: 18:35 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 12 November 2026

Morgan Rogers has rubbished questions around team-mate and friend Cole Palmer's commitment to England after the Chelsea star was left out of the latest squad.

After missing out on selection for the World Cup, Palmer was called up to the group for the first international break of the season as he continued to monitor his fitness, but dropped out of the squad.

It meant he was again ignored when it came to selection for this fortnight's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, with manager Thomas Tuchel saying Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him.

The events have led to criticism of Palmer, who scored for England in the final of Euro 2024, but Rogers has moved to defend his friend.

'It's a lie,' Rogers, who was speaking after starting and scoring for England in their 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday, said on BBC 5 Live. 'He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

'We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he's been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn't?

Morgan Rogers (right) has rubbished questions around Cole Palmer's (left) commitment to the England team

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel (right) said Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him

'But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 to 15 years, (so) he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

'It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it. But it's something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.'

Tuchel has accepted that Palmer is 'no exception' to being 'desperate' to wanting to play for England.

But the German claimed he has largely opted to stick with much of the group he ran with in the last international break, despite calling up Jobe Bellingham, James Hill, and Josh King – who plays in Palmer's position – for the first time.

'It's not personal,' the Three Lions boss said on the 24-year-old's omission. 'And of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.'

Rogers, though, is desperate to see Palmer back in an England shirt.

'What a player he is,' he added. 'What a person he is and it's someone you want to see in an England shirt.

'He's got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what we can do, what he's done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.'

#1958. Mauricio Pochettino drops big tactics hint in first interview as Manchester United manager

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Mauricio Pochettino says he wants the Manchester United squad to feel "free" when playing in the new manager's first hint at his tactical approach.

Pochettino arrived at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday and on Thursday took charge of his first training session. On Sunday comes his first game, away at Anfield against Liverpool.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be tasked with dragging Man Utd out of the relegation zone and back into the top echelons of English football.

The now-sacked Michael Carrick oversaw the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, and much of the malaise was put down to his tactical setups and a lack of energy from the players on the pitch.

And Pochettino, who is known for his hard drills in training, wants to bring the energy back to his players.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino told the club's official website.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

We need to love the players that we have, we need to support the players

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

On the significance of culture to success, he adds: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”

Arsenal have reportedly joined the race for Paris Saint-Germain defender David Boly, who is still waiting to sign his first professional contract. According to Le Parisien, the Premier League side want to disrupt the plans of PSG sporting adviser Luis Campos, with talks with the 17-year-old’s representatives expected in the coming weeks.

Boly has no shortage of suitors. After Eintracht Frankfurt and Bayer Leverkusen, a Premier League heavyweight is said to have come forward in recent days in an attempt to take him away from Paris Saint-Germain.

Boly came on as a substitute for the first time this season against Troyes on 30 October, in a 1-0 win. He then made his Champions League debut away at Villarreal in a 6-0 win and certainly made his mark, scoring PSG’s sixth goal from a pass by Joao Neves. That match was part of an 11-game winning run for the club, and the result stood out among a run of dominant displays before the international break.

There is no doubt that his playing time should increase steadily in the second half of the season, particularly as the Paris club have shown their desire to keep him by offering a first professional contract with a very high financial proposal, according to L’Equipe. Even so, PSG will need to complete the signing quickly, because several clubs are interested in the teenager. Top Mercato reported that a Bundesliga club had made him a priority.

According to Le Parisien, Arsenal have added themselves to the list for the signing of the right-back and intend to frustrate Campos’s plans. Boly appears for now to be prioritising PSG, however. In the longer term, he could become the back-up to Achraf Hakimi on the right side of defence.

That role fits what PSG are looking for. Earlier this month it was reported that the French champions’ main defensive priorities are a right-sided centre-back and a right-back to cover for Hakimi, rather than a left-back. A homegrown teenager already in the squad would solve part of that problem at no transfer cost, which makes a quick agreement more important.

In all likelihood, the Paris hierarchy and the player should agree the basis of a five-year contract. But Eintracht Frankfurt, Bayer Leverkusen and Arsenal will be waiting in the wings if the negotiations fail. The pressure is therefore on Campos and his team to secure the deal before the rival clubs make their formal approaches.

#1955. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final?

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1954. England 2-1 Croatia PLAYER RATINGS: Whose position is under 'serious' threat? Which two regulars need to show more? And who was at the heart of Three Lions' best attacking play?

Published: 17:06 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:16 EST, 12 November 2026

Harry Kane scored on his record 126th appearance for England as they beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley in the Nations League.

The Bayern Munich striker, 33, scored his 92nd goal for the Three Lions from the penalty spot to give them the victory.

Morgan Rogers had opened the scoring in the first half before Petar Sucic equalised.

Thomas Tuchel's side go to Spain on Sunday, where they will be in a shoot-out to qualify for the League A finals.

CRAIG HOPE was at Wembley to bring you our player ratings.

Harry Kane scored on his landmark 126th England outing to give them a 2-1 win over Croatia

Was left exposed for goal and not much he could do. Made four fairly routine saves and kicking was fine. Tuchel says he’s the No.1 but that will only become apparent should he start in Spain on Sunday. It feels like his position is under serious threat from James Trafford, not that he did anything wrong here.

A very bright start, including one delightful drop in behind for Rogers, but he faded thereafter. Not the creative force he should be in a game like this and questions remain over both Alexander-Arnold’s current level of performance and whether anyone will emerge as England’s first-choice right back.

He was enjoying a trouble-free night until mistake leading to Croatia equaliser with baffling decision to head back to Pickford amid crowded goalmouth. He did, in part, make amends by winning penalty for Kane goal, as well as timely late slide to block shot. Doesn’t convince as a starter, though.

Like Quansah, all was going well until Croatia goal, and he’ll be disappointed not to get the first header on the corner before ball dropped. He looked shaky after that and was nearly outdone for a Croatia equaliser late on. Could have done with a breather after 70 minutes or so given recent return from injury.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was not the creative force he should have been in a game like this

In a position that is up for grabs he did his chances no harm at all and was the pick of the backline by far. Got forward at every opportunity and rarely wasted a ball. Was also there at the other end with several key interceptions. A solid night.

A lot of huff and puff but, as too often in an England shirt, not enough to show for it by way of creation or penetration. With some bright young midfielders like James Garner and Alex Scott emerging, Rice has to do more, you feel, to make sure he stays in the XI. This was an underwhelming night in that regard.

Lots of involvement and omnipresent across the park, as ever. One superb dribble that drew applause, but we need to see more of that inspiration higher up the pitch. A good display, but no chances created. Partnership with Rice still feels a little forced at times.

Morgan Rogers was his team's brightest player when he forced the opening goal

Was already his team’s brightest player when he forced opening goal with close-range finish. Clearly a man in form and brought that brightness to this stage. With doubts over Saka’s durability, he looks the best bet as the starting right winger. Was at the heart of all good about England in final third.

Provided assist with confident cushion for pal Rogers and he was a threat throughout, even if final shot or pass didn’t quite come off, the assist apart. Felt like he was in second gear a little, especially knowing booking would have ruled him out of Spain on Sunday in his home city of Madrid.

Didn’t happen for Barcelona winger and he’ll know he should have done better when twice cutting in on right foot and having a good sight at goal. He missed the target on both occasions. Gordon can’t get cosy knowing he’s Tuchel’s first choice on the left, and more is needed.

Anthony Gordon will know he should have done better - he can't get cosy on the left flank

The quarterback! Was this a glimpse of the future? Kane operated even deeper than he usually does at times and one long-range pass from 30 yards inside his own half drew gasps from the Wembley crowd. It was his playmaker’s dink in behind that led to opener. Got his goal with penalty dink on his big night.

Ben White (on for Alexander-Arnold 78) - 6

A win, but it was not comfortable and Tuchel leaves this with yet more questions about how he builds a defence for the European Championship. A sold-out Wembley weren’t exactly thrilled by England’s attack, either. Job done, but it was dull.

#1953. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino's £83m offer to 'great' Barcelona star as possible Bruno Fernandes replacement

By Lewis Nolan | 17 Nov 2026 23:33

Manchester United have launched an £83m bid for Barcelona attacker Fermin Lopez despite interest from teams like Chelsea, the latest report has revealed.

The Red Devils will begin a new era under boss Mauricio Pochettino on Sunday, when they take on rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

A loss in that Premier League clash could leave the club last in the table, and if the team are to avoid a prolonged relegation battle, they must quickly accumulate points.

However, United have only scored 14 goals in their first 10 top-flight outings this campaign, and their lack of firepower could prove costly.

Spanish outlet Sport claim that the Red Devils have made a bid worth £83m to Barcelona for attacker Lopez, though so have Chelsea.

Lopez has been in fine form for Barca this season, scoring eight goals and registering seven assists in 15 matches, while he scored 13 goals and provided 17 assists in 48 games in 2025-26.

The Spaniard is capable of playing in a variety of roles across the frontline, including as a striker, but he has often been deployed in an advanced role behind Raphinha by Hansi Flick this term.

There is no doubt that Lopez would strengthen the squad, but committing at least £83m to one player would arguably be the wrong move.

The Red Devils have gaps in several areas of their squad, especially in defence and out wide, and the 23-year-old should not be signed at the expense of other targets.

One of the reasons Lopez may have emerged as a target could be due to the uncertain future of captain Bruno Fernandes, whose contract will expire at the end of the current campaign unless United activate their option to extend his deal for another year.

The 32-year-old has often been criticised for his reckless pressing, something that could impact Pochettino's aggressive system.

Lopez is excellent out of possession, and the fact that United have been linked to the Spaniard could hint at the club's desire to move on from Fernandes.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League have frequently been linked with the Portuguese international, and it would not be surprising if the Red Devils extended Fernandes's contract before selling him in the summer transfer window.

#1952. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

#1951. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#1950. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

#1948. Majority of clubs vote for extra legal protection for Premier League chiefs

Premier League board members have been given extra legal protection amid the threat of actions linked to the Manchester City case.

Eighteen clubs are reported to have supported changes to the league’s articles at a clubs meeting in central London on Thursday, which extend protections provided to individual board members to enable them to freely carry out their duties.

A 14-club majority is required for votes to be carried, and it was understood to have been comfortably above that.

The change comes after City sponsor Etihad said in September it was considering legal action over the “damaging” implications of the independent commission’s guilty verdict against the club.

The airline was not named in the verdict, which found City had benefited from “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and disguise costs to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules. City have appealed against the verdict. Another City sponsor, Etisalat, was reported by The Times to be considering similar action earlier this week.

The Press Association understands the issue was brought to a vote in order to bring the league’s individual legal cover in line with similar companies – including many of its clubs – and that these articles had not been looked at since the league’s inception in 1992.

There was no indication of any cap on the costs clubs could be exposed to as a result of the change to the league’s articles, and no wider discussion or questions raised on the City case despite this being the first shareholders’ meeting since the verdict was published on September 29.

Club executives also received a first update of the season from referees’ chief Howard Webb.

He is understood to have accepted the 10th round of matches immediately before the November international break had been especially difficult.

Six on-field errors were identified by the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel which were not corrected by VAR intervention.

This is in part due to the high bar for intervention being operated this season, where referee’s on-field calls can only be overturned where it is felt the error was not a clear and obvious one.

#1947. Prince William leads tributes to Harry Kane as England captain breaks appearance record with 126th cap: Royal presents star with shirt marking occasion as Wembley celebrates milestone

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 14:45 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026

Prince William led tributes for Harry Kane as Wembley honoured the England captain on reaching his record-breaking 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

Kane, who became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or last month, celebrated another remarkable feat as he surpassed legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history.

After walking out with his four children for kick-off, followed by his England team-mates, the Bayern Munich forward first held his Ballon d'Or trophy aloft to Wembley's buoyant crowd, soaking up the celebrations.

Shilton approached the England captain to present him with a medal displaying his achievement, before Kane's former Spurs team-mate Luka Modric continued the tributes by offering him another gift.

Prince William then walked on to the pitch to shake Kane's hand and present him with a framed shirt, bearing the words 'Kane 126'.

As well as holding the record for England's most capped player, the 33-year-old striker is also England's highest ever scorer with 91 goals, ahead of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton who netted 53 and 49 respectively during their careers.

Prince William shakes Harry Kane's hand as he celebrates the England captain's record cap

The Prince led tributes as Wembley honoured Kane ahead of England's clash with Croatia

Kane, accompanied by his four children on the pitch, held his Ballon d'Or aloft to supporters

Prince William applauded 'brilliant and remarkable' Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph with a personal social media message after the ceremony in London.

The Prince of Wales, signing his message off with his personal 'W' initial, posted on Instagram: 'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Kane, who has been widely regarded as a model professional and humble superstar during his career, admitted he still has an ego of sorts in an interview on the eve of his record-breaking England cap.

Asked if he has an ego, Kane replied: ‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!

'But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

On becoming England's highest appearance maker, he joked that some of his current Three Lions team-mates might catch his total by the end of their careers.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ he added. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!

He has passed Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history - with 126 to his name

Kane receives a gift from ex-Spurs team-mate and fellow Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric

’In football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better.

'While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

#1945. JJ Gabriel to Real Madrid: Watch farewell message as Man United receive criticism for teenager's transfer exit

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 00:11

JJ Gabriel has posted a farewell message to Manchester United fans ahead of his impending switch to Real Madrid.

Mauricio Pochettino has not taken charge of a single training session as head coach of the club, but one of his first tasks will be to deal with the fallout of a damaging exit.

Teenager Gabriel revealed in September that he wished to move away from Old Trafford, and while he was registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving to a club in the European Union once he turned 16.

A number of sides were reported to be interested in signing him, but Real Madrid have seemingly won the race for his signature.

Gabriel has confirmed his exit from United in a farewell video message posted to his Instagram page on Tuesday.

??? JJ Gabriel: “Goodbye and thank you, Man United”. https://t.co/5uXeBLHIcX

Though there have been many reasons to be critical of United's approach to their young stars, it would be harsh to reprimand them over losing Gabriel.

It was reported earlier this year that the teenager and his entourage were disappointed about the pathway into first-team football, but the youngster only turned 16 on October 6.

Perhaps Gabriel believed he should have been fast-tracked into the XI like Lamine Yamal was at Barcelona and Spain, but the Baca winger's progression into senior football was anomalous.

It should also be noted that he will have to battle against the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in Real Madrid's team, so it remains to be seen if he is given the minutes he desires.

Though United have not necessarily conducted themselves poorly in regard to Gabriel's exit, the saga may have an unfortunate impact on their image as a fruitful hub for young talent.

United are currently engulfed in a relegation battle in the Premier League, and the atmosphere at Old Trafford has arguably never been more toxic.

The failures of the team on the pitch and the chaos behind the scenes may deter younger talents from joining United in the future, though the club's hierarchy will hope that Pochettino can restore the club's place as a premier destination.

AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment, could be publicly listed within five years according to a report.

As Cardinale himself said, there will be several new revenue streams that ultimately will benefit the football club, making it possible to invest more money in players and additional infrastructure. In short, it’s a big project and it could get even bigger.

#1942. Troyes vs Le Havre - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 18 Nov 2026 02:01

The bottom two teams in Ligue 1 will kick off matchday 11 of the campaign Friday as Troyes welcome Le Havre to Stade de l’Aube

Heading into this match, Troyes are 17th in the table after suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, putting them six points above the Normandy club, who lost their last league fixture 2-0 at home to Lorient.

Some improved results of late have brought Troyes back within reach of Ligue 1 safety after 10 matchdays in the top flight.

After losing five successive matches in this competition, Stephane Dumont has seen his side earn points in two of their last three contests.

One of the biggest improvements has been their poise at the back, as they have collected two clean sheets in their last three league fixtures after conceding multiple goals in five straight games.

While their defensive game is much improved, they are still struggling to create many scoring opportunities, sitting dead last in the league for big chances so far.

On Friday, they can claim consecutive Ligue 1 triumphs at Stade de l’Aube for the first time since March-April 2022, after beating Le Mans on Halloween (2-0).

ESTAC have won three of their last four home meetings with Le Havre, all in Ligue 2, and have lost just one of their last five games against them.

It is an urgent time for Le Havre, who enter this matchday six points back of Ligue 1 safety and are the only side yet to win this season.

The club have said that this is an emergency situation and, as such, appointed Valerien Ismael as the new manager in hopes of getting out of the relegation zone.

The well-travelled coach, who was born in Strasbourg, has a reputation for turning clubs around quickly, taking Barnsley from a team near the bottom of the Championship to a playoff position by the end of the 2020-21 campaign.

Ismael has a big job ahead of him, to transform a side in Le Havre, who have given up the joint-second-most goals in Ligue 1 thus far (22).

He takes over a team that have suffered six consecutive defeats in this competition, while earning just one point away from home this season.

While they have not fared well against Troyes of late, Le Ciel et Marine are unbeaten against them in Ligue 1 this century, winning that last meeting in Normandy in 2003 (1-0).

Due to an ankle injury, Troyes are expected to be without Anis Ouzenadji on Friday, and Yacouba Kone is dealing with a sore knee.

From matchday nine to 10, we saw two new faces in their starting 11, with Ismael Boura and Kandet Diawara replacing Paolo Gozzi and Timothe Nkada, while Hillel Konate got the start between the sticks yet again.

As for Le Havre, Rassoul Ndiaye and Elias Jelert are doubtful because of leg injuries, while Timothee Pembele is dealing with adductor pain and unlikely to feature.

Lionel Mpasi and Felix Mambimbi are out with Achilles tendon ruptures, while Stephan Zagadou is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Bodart; Sasso, Koffi, Touba; Ouziad, Ebonog, Mwanga, Richardson; Fofana, Samatta; Maja

Ismael has a reputation for elevating his teams quickly, and against a Troyes side that are not terribly potent in front of goal, we believe the Normandy club will catch a break and pull out a narrow victory.

Pochettino will also hope to be able to call upon longer-term absentees Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford this weekend, with some reports suggesting they will finally be ready to return from muscle and hip problems, respectively. It is unclear whether either man trained on Thursday.

Pochettino will deliver a more detailed team news update when he faces the media for the first time as United boss on Friday afternoon.
