#1921. Man City transfer news: La Liga giant abandons pursuit of Josko Gvardiol

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:40

Barcelona’s winter transfer window is becoming seriously complicated, with sporting director Deco reportedly forced to abandon a second defensive target after Jonathan Tah. Hansi Flick has clearly expressed his desire for defensive reinforcements, but the priority deals appear difficult to complete.

La Liga leaders Barcelona have seen their lead over Real Madrid shrink in recent weeks, with Jose Mourinho’s side now only three points behind after 12 games.

The title race is expected to be fiercely contested this season and the Catalans will need reinforcements to achieve their objectives. The stated winter priority is to sign a centre-back, but finding the perfect profile, at the right price, is no easy task.

Deco and Barcelona’s hierarchy have positioned themselves for Alessandro Bastoni, among others, but the chances of completing his arrival are slim. In recent days, the Tah option has also closed, as Bayern Munich have no intention of letting him leave. Now another deal can be forgotten about at Barcelona, the one leading to Josko Gvardiol.

According to information gathered by AS, the Manchester City defender matched the profile Barcelona are looking for, namely a centre-back capable of playing at left-back.

The problem is that the Croatia international has extended his contract with Manchester City until 2031 and a transfer ‘seems impossible’, the Spanish outlet reports.

Possible financial or sporting sanctions threatening Manchester City could have eventually unblocked the situation, but nothing will be announced before 2027. The Catalans therefore find themselves somewhat in an impasse, and signing the two or three priority defensive targets is becoming seriously complicated.

Barcelona’s hierarchy will probably have to aim a little lower, particularly as the budget is far from unlimited in Catalonia. The sale of Alejandro Balde, reportedly set to leave, could however swell the winter transfer budget.

#1920. Watch: Pulisic shines as Pochettino news dominates headlines – Captain America bags a brace vs. Haiti

Last night, AC Milan will have been very happy to see Christian Pulisic extending his fine goalscoring form with a brace for America.

The United States national team have certainly faced a rocky few days. Thanks to Manchester United parting ways with Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role as the head coach of the project after the international break, leaving them in a strange position currently.

However, that was not a problem for The Stars and The Stripes, who put six past Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League. Of course, who else would be key but Pulisic himself?

Playing as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system – which will have pleased Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim – Pulisic was instrumental, scoring a brace in just two minutes. After 62 minutes, he stepped up from the spot after drawing the penalty himself.

Then, just a minute later, he added a second and recorded his 35th goal for the USMNT in 91 appearances.

For the attacker, it extends his fine run of form and the second half of 2026 is proving to be much more fruitful than the first. In Serie A, he’s scored four goals and provided an assist in eight games, and he’s now grabbed two more for the national team. After missing the last camp, it’s another reminder of his importance.

With Pochettino departing, it’s clear that they’ll still be in fine hands, with Pulisic remaining key!

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

A few notes: 1. This first match (of two for the Nations League) was played in Miami, Florida, and counted as a home match for Haiti, as the ongoing gang violence in Haiti made it too dangerous for an international match to be played there.

2. South Florida has a very large Haitian population, and as a result, the stadium looked like it was 90% filled with Haitians and fans of Haiti. So yeah, it was a home match for Haiti.

3. Haiti can be a very physical and challenging team to play against, but two things helped here – they were missing something like five of their starters from their World Cup team, and the ref was actually somewhat decent in calling fouls properly, instead of the usual CONCACAF ref who lets everything go and turns the match into a mixed martial arts no holds barred cage fight.

4. It was only 1-0 at halftime, Haiti was pressing very hard and were very physical. But then they just collapsed after the foul on Pulisic and the PK.

5. The USMNT has never looked this good – as a longtime follower of the USMNT, I can clearly see Pochettino’s influence and his selection of players and his tactics finally coming into fruition. Too bad he is leaving.

6. Poch’s coaching, tactics, and selection of younger players actually look a lot like what Amorim is doing at Milan. And yes, in his first year with the USMNT, Poch took some losses to teams that the USMNT had been able to beat previously. Which should mean that Amorim’s system should start looking great next year.

7. Unfortunately for Pochettino, ManUre are completely packed with players on high wages that are poorly suited for his tactics. As ManUre are in a relegation fight and Poch generally takes at least a year to rebuild a team and fully implement his ideas, I would not be at all be surprised to see ManUre get relegated. Poch is not a specialist in fighting relegation.

Yes, finally a decent ref and a decent field for a Hati home game.

#1919. Trafford’s England heroics come as no surprise to Leeds boss Farke

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Daniel Farke admitted he was surprised that everyone was so shocked by James Trafford's display during England's thrilling Nations League win over Spain.

Trafford was selected to start ahead of the Three Lions' final Group A3 fixture against the reigning world champions, and he more than played his part in their 3-2 victory.

England were three goals ahead thanks to strikes from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White before Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal.

Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams were able to find a way past the Leeds goalkeeper, but in the latter stages at the Metropolitano, Trafford produced a string of important stops, including a superb double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte.

But Trafford's display did not come as a shock to Farke, whose Leeds side have conceded just eight Premier League goals so far this season.

Only Arsenal (five) and Brighton (seven) have let in fewer, while Trafford has made the second-most saves (37) and has the best save ratio (81.4%) in the competition in 2026-27.

"I'm a bit bored because in my last 237 press conferences I've been praising him and right now the whole country is praising him," Farke said of Trafford.

"I'm surprised that everyone is so surprised that our goalkeeper is capable of delivering a top performance. That is why he wears the gloves.

"I also expect him to catch some balls and make some saves. I'm not surprised he's had a good performance."

Trafford will expect to busy again this weekend when Leeds make the trip to Stamford Bridge to face a Chelsea side who signed off for the international break with a defeat.

Enzo Le Fee's first-half penalty was enough to earn Sunderland a 1-0 win, a result that saw Xabi Alonso's side drop out of the top four at the expense of Liverpool.

Valentin Barco was an unused substitute at the Stadium of Light and was unable to see any minutes for Argentina in their defeat to Uruguay and 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica.

Barco has only made four Premier League appearances for Chelsea this season, totalling 119 minutes, but he believes he will eventually come good at Stamford Bridge.

"As a player, you always want to play so you are not happy when you don't, but I understand this is the best national team in the world," Barco told ESPN.

"But I'm happy to come to the national team, to continue to represent my country. I will now try to play at Chelsea and contribute."

"I think I can give a lot more. I also said the same thing when I was at Strasbourg; even when I was playing well, I knew I could give more because I know what I can give.

"I have a lot of confidence in myself, so I have to keep working to continue growing."

Only Joao Pedro (eight) has more goal involvements than Rogers in the Premier League for Chelsea this season (six – five goals, one assist), but after an encouraging international break with England, he will be full of confidence.

Rogers also boasts a good record against Leeds in the top-flight. Only against Manchester United and Bournemouth (both three) has he netted more times against than Leeds (two, level with four other teams).

Of the players to play 500+ minutes since the start of February, only Benjamin Sesko (one every 83 minutes) has a better minutes-per-goal ratio in the Premier League than Okafor, who has netted eight goals in 894 minutes of action (one every 112 minutes).

He has also now scored eight goals across his last 16 Premier League appearances, having netted just two in his first 21 in the competition.

Beautiful scenes! https://t.co/GYpuRXqBZi

Chelsea have won eight of their last 10 home games against Leeds in all competitions (D2) since a 2-0 loss in December 1999. They have already beaten the Whites 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in the EFL Cup this season.

The Blues have also won 10 points from five top-flight home games this season (W3 D1 L1), their most after five home matches since 2022-23 under Thomas Tuchel/Graham Potter (11), and their most at the start of a campaign under a new manager since 2018-19 under Maurizio Sarri (11).

But this could be an intriguing battle at both ends of the pitch. Leeds have generated the most expected goals (xG) from set-pieces (excl. penalties) in the Premier League this season (6.1), with their only two goals across their last four league games coming from a throw-in and a corner.

Chelsea, meanwhile, have conceded the second-most goals from set-pieces (eight) in the big five European leagues in 2026-27 (Monza – nine, excluding penalties).

Leeds avoided defeat in both Premier League meetings with Chelsea last season (3-1 home, 2-2 away), last going unbeaten in three in a row against the Blues between November 2000 and October 2001.

However, Leeds have won just one of their last 25 matches in London in all competitions (D6 L18), a 3-0 win at Millwall in September 2023. Four of their last five defeats have come in the capital, including two against Chelsea: 1-0 at Wembley in the FA Cup in April and 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in September.

#1918. Chelsea injury news: Moises Caicedo concern grows after Ecuador half-time withdrawal

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30

Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

Despite Xabi Alonso acknowledging that the midfielder was carrying a fitness issue into the game at Sunderland before the November international break, Caicedo played the full 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light.

Prior to representing his country across two matches, the Blues star himself admitted that he was not fully fit, yet intended to feature in both games.

As well as playing 84 minutes against Costa Rica at the weekend, Caicedo featured for 45 minutes versus Bolivia on Tuesday night.

However, it has since been revealed that the 25-year-old requested to be withdrawn at half time.

Speaking to reporter Johanna Calderon after the Bolivia match, Caicedo suggested that he did not want to risk his fitness in the second half.

In an video posted on X, he said: "I wasn’t feeling too well, so I asked to come off.

"I have another commitment with my club, so I’m trying to get there as soon as possible and recover."

Not only does Caicedo now face a long-haul flight from Ecuador, he is giving up five hours of recovery due to the time difference between Guayaquil and London.

When you factor in tiredness to add to the injury issue that he is currently trying to protect, Caicedo should not be starting the game with Leeds.

Jordan Henderson was not called up by England, whereas Romeo Lavia played on Sunday night having missed Belgium's first of two UEFA Nations game during the international break.

Starting that pair and having Caicedo on the substitutes' bench is the only scenario that makes sense for Alonso.

#1917. Maldini admits career could’ve been different without father and Liedholm: “Liked playing goalkeeper”

Things could’ve been much different for Paolo Maldini at AC Milan without two major figures in his life and career.

Maldini has two faces at Milan, but both remain adored by the fanbase. Firstly, you have the legendary defender, whose number was retired with him, a sign of respect and a chance to honour a career and legacy which surpasses many in the game.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, he returned as the sporting director, ending the Scudetto drought. Of course, that story didn’t have an ending as romantic as his playing career, but his legacy lives on. In fact, he may be voted into the Hall of Fame in the very near future.

Speaking to Tuttomercatoweb, via PianetaMilan, Maldini looked at the earliest stages of his career, as well as when he really took off for the Rossoneri.

“When my father took me to try out for AC Milan, I liked playing goalkeeper, but luckily I ended up choosing to be a defender. I played football with my friends in the park and at the youth club: I didn’t feel like I was destined for success at all, and until the day I made my debut, I never thought I could reach the highest levels.

“My dad always told me that the most important thing is to have fun, because if you treat it only as a job, it loses its magic.”

“There’s one person in particular who believed in me and wanted me to play when I was 15: Nils Liedholm, then AC Milan’s coach. He loved showing his faith in young players, and once, during a break, he asked me whether I preferred to play on the right or left. I replied that it was obviously his choice, but it was a gesture that helped me a lot.”

As they say, one change and the rest is history. With Maldini, that was certainly the case.

#1916. Chelsea injury news: Xabi Alonso in double boost ahead of Leeds United showdown

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:58

Chelsea have been handed a double injury boost ahead after Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino both represented Argentina on Tuesday night.

Martinez and Anselmino were called up by Lionel Scaloni despite spending weeks and months on the sidelines.

While goalkeeper Martinez had been unavailable with a fractured jaw since October 17, Anselmino has not played any competitive minutes for Chelsea in 2026-27 due to a hamstring injury.

However, the pair featured as Argentina cruised to a 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in Cordoba.

Starting between the sticks wearing a protective mask, Martinez played the full 90 minutes, albeit only having to make two saves during a one-sided contest.

Meanwhile, Anselmino was introduced as a 71st-minute substitute as the former world champions saw out the win.

Anselmino's outing - his first for Argentina - is particularly notable because it is his first since a 29-minute appearance in a pre-season friendly versus Johor DT on August 9.

When Moises Caicedo has provided a further fitness concern for Xabi Alonso, having Martinez and Anselmino come through unscathed for Argentina is a welcome boost.

Alonso must now decide whether to retain Mike Penders for Saturday's Premier League game with Leeds United or hand an immediate recall to Martinez.

Given the time difference and Penders having largely impressed in his absence, Martinez may expect to be named on the substitutes' bench.

Although it is possible that Anselmino will not feature in Chelsea's squad versus Leeds, Alonso requires an extra central-defensive option due to Maxence Lacroix being expected to be sidelined until January.

Realistically, the 21-year-old could be handed a start for the Blues' Under-21s ranks before coming into contention for the first team.

#1915. Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'

It's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

The treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their new training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

It’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is said to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.

#1913. Man United transfer news: Major new rival emerges in race for Alejandro Balde

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 10:15

Lacking game time at Barcelona, Alejandro Balde is looking for a way out in January, with Paris Saint-Germain only just appearing in the picture.

Alejandro Balde is set to be one of the talking points of the winter transfer window. Struggling at Barcelona, where his game time has fallen considerably, the 23-year-old left-back is considering leaving to find a bigger role elsewhere.

His record this season is particularly meagre, with five appearances and only 124 minutes played. It is a situation that contrasts sharply with the status the Spaniard enjoyed in Catalonia until very recently.

According to the latest information from Spain and Italy, several clubs are following his situation. Juventus are considering a loan, while Monaco are eyeing a bigger move. Now Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United have also entered the fray.

Manchester United are reportedly going all out to sign Balde in January.

According to TEAMtalk, the club’s recruitment department believes the left-back has a high ceiling and Barcelona are open to a loan, which would allow Manchester United to assess him before committing to a permanent deal.

The same report says Balde is willing to move to the Premier League and that his relationship with Barcelona manager Hansi Flick is ‘completely broken and glacial’.

Fabrizio Romano has described the chance of a January exit as ‘serious and concrete’, adding that Balde is ‘genuinely ready to consider leaving’ and exploring options with his agent, Jorge Mendes. Manchester United were interested in the summer but did not proceed, with Balde considered too expensive for a left-back, in talks said to have involved a fee of €50m-€55m (£42.5m-£46.5m) and a net salary of more than €5m (£4.3m).

Valued at around €40m (£34m), the Barcelona player represents a market opportunity for Paris Saint-Germain. At 23, Balde already has significant experience at the highest level and still has room for improvement.

Quick and explosive, he fits the profile of a modern full-back and offers better guarantees than Lucas Digne, the disappointing summer signing. His ability to get in behind and create overloads would give Luis Enrique’s team another attacking dimension, and the move could also be a fresh start for a player who has lost confidence and continuity at Barcelona, not least because Luis Enrique rotates his starting line-up heavily.

The main obstacle is Nuno Mendes, who owns the left-back position at Paris Saint-Germain and is one of the best players in the world in that role, if not the best.

At 24, the Portuguese is a major part of the club’s project, and the left-footed Balde cannot play on the right side of defence, unless the manager comes up with something.

Luis Enrique also generally prefers a right-footed winger on the left, so Paris Saint-Germain could sign an excellent player without offering him a lasting prospect of starting, with a real risk of frustration.

#1911. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

“They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

It’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7

What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

City chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

Arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was important to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ

00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh

Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

Then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

Foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

The Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

City soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

Considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

That’s certainly one way to start a new season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

With no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I said already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

[Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

[What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

[On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the big margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

Elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

#1910. Man United's Bruno Fernandes hailed by Portuguese media for his "captain's performance" in Portugal win over Wales

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:27, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:29

Bruno Fernandes helped Portugal record a 3-2 victory over Wales in the UEFA Nations League on Tuesday night, with the Manchester United captain in strong form.

The attacker actually made the breakthrough in the Nations League clash, scoring in the 11th minute, but Portugal ultimately had to come from 2-1 behind to triumph.

Portugal comfortably secured a spot in the quarter-finals of the Nations League courtesy of their first-placed finish in Group 4 of League A on 15 points.

Fernandes' attention will now switch back to club affairs, as he looks to help Man United beat Liverpool on Sunday in what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils.

The 32-year-old should be in a good place entering that match given his strong performance for the national side on Tuesday night.

Bruno Fernandes scored his 30th goal for Portugal on his 99th appearance. ?? His game by numbers vs. Wales: 89 minutes played 80 touches 56/67 successful passes 15 passes into final third 4/5 duels won 4/7 accurate long balls 3 tackles 2 chances created 2 clearances 2x possessions won 1/1 shots on target 1 goal MOTM performance. ⭐️

As expected, the Portuguese media were full of praise for Fernandes after the Wales game.

PortuGOAL said that Fernandes put in a "captain's performance" against Wales, with the Man United star impressing from both an offensive and defensive point of view, and he was handed an overall rating of 8/10.

ZeroZero called Fernandes "decisive" and praised the attacker for helping Portugal to navigate their way through the latter stages after being reduced to 10 men; he was handed a rating of 7.8/10.

A Bola focused on Fernandes' stunning goal in the early stages and also praised his passing ability, having set up chances for both Joao Cancelo and Goncalo Ramos.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough campaign for Man United, who currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table.

Fernandes has been far from his best for most of the campaign, but he has still managed to come up with six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the club this term.

There is currently speculation surrounding Fernandes' future at Old Trafford, with the Portuguese allegedly turning down the latest offer from Man United to renew his contract.

Fernandes is allegedly waiting to see what direction the club move in under Pochettino before making any firm decisions on his future with the 20-time English champions.

#1909. ‘I tried everything’ to convince Guimaraes to stay at Newcastle, says Jaissle

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Matthias Jaissle conceded Bruno Guimaraes' mind was already made up on joining Arsenal despite trying his hardest to keep the Brazilian at Newcastle United.

Guimaraes is set to return to St. James' Park for the first time since completing his reported £75m transfer to the Premier League champions in the summer.

He joined Newcastle from Lyon in 2022 and went on to make 195 appearances across all competitions, scoring 31 goals and providing 31 assists for the Magpies.

The 29-year-old also captained Newcastle to their first domestic trophy in 70 years in the EFL Cup last March, but he made his intentions clear of an exit after last season.

Since joining Arsenal, Guimaraes has played 14 times across all competitions and scored two goals, one of which came against Newcastle's rivals Sunderland.

"I met him shortly in pre-season, but his decision was already made to join Arsenal," Jaissle said when asked about the missed opportunity of working with Guimaraes.

"I tried my best, but the decision was made, so now we are opponents and competitors. Our approach is to give not only him, but also his team-mates, a difficult 90 minutes.

"I just said that we counted on him as a leader last year. I tried to explain the role he would've had with us, but again the decision was already made before I even spoke with him.

"I felt it was my job to do my best anyway, at least then I can look in the mirror and say: 'I tried everything'."

When asked about the reception Guimaraes should receive on his return to St. James' Park, Jaissle said: "That's not something I should influence. I don't have thoughts on that."

Back to business at St. James' Park on Saturday! https://t.co/VDGwD9Jx7c

— Newcastle United (@NUFC) November 18, 2026

Newcastle signed off for the international break with a 1-1 draw away to Fulham, a result that leaves them 12th in the table after 10 games of the season.

The Magpies have won just one of their last 29 Premier League games against sides starting the day top of the table (D8 L20), and none of their last 18 (D4 L14) since a 2-1 victory over Chelsea in December 2014.

Newcastle are also winless in 14 Premier League games against reigning champions (D5 L9) since beating Manchester City 2-1 in January 2019.

And their struggles this year have surprisingly come at home. No side has lost more Premier League home games in 2026 than Newcastle (seven), who have lost both of their last two at St. James' Park without scoring.

Not since February 2014 have they lost more in a row without a goal at home in the competition (run of four), but Jaissle believes the Newcastle fans could be key to beating Mikel Arteta's side.

"If you face the champions, that is motivation enough," Jaissle added. "We are playing at home in front of our fans; they can be the twelfth man.

"The fans can give us so much power and support. This is a great opportunity, a big challenge."

#1908. Reports: Milan challenging ‘Inter and half of Europe’ for 16-year-old Frankfurt star

It seems AC Milan may attempt to make two signings from Eintracht Frankfurt in the coming months, with a young star on their radar.

Milan and Frankfurt have been linked together regularly in the past year, from Markus Krösche and Timmo Hardung to Can Uzun; reports have consistently put the two together. Now, a new chapter is being written.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to Calciomercato.com, the Rossoneri are closely monitoring Niko Ilicevic. Now, it’s not a name you’re likely to have heard of unless you’re a keen fan of the Bundesliga. However, he’s the record holder for the youngest appearance-maker in the German top flight.

Born in 2010, he’s the prized jewel of the Frankfurt project and the Diavolo will be ‘a key player’ in January. Whilst they want to support Ruben Amorim, they also want to secure future talents and Ilicevic is one of them.

Bobby Gardiner has already sent scouts to watch him and Markus Krosche’s arrival could also be key. However, half of Europe are watching him. Sky Sport (whose information is included in the original report) stated that Inter were keen a few months ago, but Real Madrid, Barcelona, Arsenal, Bayern Munich and Manchester City are also in the race.

It won’t be an easy task, but Milan are at work and the waters of a potential move are already being tested…

#1907. France star Desire Doue is left with gruesome tooth injury after PSG youngster suffered elbow smash to the face during Les Bleus' dismal defeat by Italy

Published: 06:41 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 13 November 2026

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

In his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'

The French then went onto say: 'The most important thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

#1904. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31

Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England

It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record. At 16, the Englishman has already been the youngest player to score in the Premier League, to play in the Champions League and to win the English league title.

This week, he added two more marks to the list: he became the youngest player to represent the England Under-21s and, three days later, the youngest to score for the side, surpassing records that belonged to Jude Bellingham.

The question is not only how many more records he can break, but what makes Dowman such a special talent and how far his characteristics can take him. The combination of individual skill, ball carrying, strength to compete physically and understanding of the game helps to explain why he can already produce against much older opponents.

Dowman was born on 31 December 2009 and joined Arsenal as a child. His progress through the youth ranks was so rapid that, at 13, he was already playing for the Under-18s. In September 2024, aged 14 years and eight months, he made his debut in the UEFA Youth League, an Under-19 competition, and became the youngest scorer in the history of the tournament.

The midfielder began training with the first team at 14 and took part in the 2025 pre-season. In August of that year, aged 15 years and 235 days, he made his Premier League debut against Leeds United. He was the second-youngest player to appear in the competition’s history, behind only Ethan Nwaneri, his Arsenal team-mate.

In November 2025, an even more significant milestone arrived. Coming on in the 3-0 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the tournament’s history, aged 15 years and 308 days. He was also the first 15-year-old to play in the competition.

The 2025-26 season brought two more high-profile records. In March, he scored against Everton and, aged 16 years and 73 days, became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, beating James Vaughan’s mark by 197 days.

Months later, he went down in Arsenal history as the youngest player to win the Premier League. The medal came at 16 years and 144 days, when the club ended a 22-year wait for the title. In October, he received three Guinness World Records certificates for the achievements.

Now, the England Under-21s have added two more chapters. Dowman made his debut for the side against Portugal on 13 November, aged 16 years and 317 days, surpassing Bellingham’s mark as the youngest player to represent the age group. On the following Monday, he started for the first time and scored the winning goal against France, aged 16 years and 320 days. Bellingham had scored his first Under-21 goal aged 17 years and 67 days.

Records broken for Arsenal and England (born 31/12/2009)

If he scores for the senior England team before 12/11/2027, Dowman will surpass Wayne Rooney (17 years and 317 days, in 2003) as the youngest scorer for England.

Age in years (y) and days (d) on the date of each record. n/a = previous holder not confirmed by an official source. Data up to 17/11/2026.

Sources: Arsenal, Premier League, ESPN and TNT Sports

Dowman’s main characteristic is his ability to carry the ball and beat opponents. He finds it easy to receive under pressure, shield possession with his body and change direction in tight spaces. He does not rely on straight-line speed alone: he uses feints, changes of pace and short movements to unbalance defenders.

Dowman already had a physique that allowed him to compete with older players, but he has also developed an intelligent way of using his body to protect the ball. That explains why he does not seem so intimidated when facing professional defenders.

Left-footed, he usually plays on the right, from where he can cut inside and use his dominant foot. The position also allows him to receive wide, draw the opposing full-back and choose between accelerating towards the box, combining with a team-mate or finding a pass inside. His ball control and ability to change the direction of play make him a particularly difficult threat to handle one-on-one.

But reducing him to a dribbling winger would ignore an important part of his repertoire. Dowman also has experience playing as an attacking midfielder and in deeper roles. In the youth ranks, he even played as a deep-lying midfielder. This variety helped him develop a broader understanding of space and the different roles on the pitch.

That versatility is an advantage for Arteta. At Arsenal, Dowman has already been used on the right and in central positions. When he receives between the lines, he can turn quickly and carry the ball towards the opposition defence. If he starts wide, he can attack the space between full-back and centre-back, moving closer to the box to shoot or take part in a combination.

There are also signs that his play without the ball matches his technical quality. In the win over France, Lee Carsley highlighted the teenager’s defensive performance, as he dropped back to intercept a pass and joined the pressing of opponents. A willingness to recover, press and take part in collective actions is an important requirement for earning a place in a side like Arteta’s.

Dowman’s rise inevitably prompts comparisons. His path recalls, in some respects, that of Nwaneri, who also made his Arsenal debut very young and had to find space in a competitive squad. Both came through the youth ranks playing in central positions, but had their first opportunities in the first team on the right.

The difference is that Dowman seems to have an even clearer ability to carry the ball at speed and beat opponents one-on-one. That does not mean it is possible to determine who will have the more successful career.

Arsenal also have reason to manage expectations. The recent episode against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup highlighted one area of concern. After suffering a heavy challenge, the teenager reacted and was sent off, receiving a three-match ban. Arteta criticised the player publicly and said professional football is not an environment protected from provocation and the consequences of one’s own actions.

There is also the question of workload. A player who starts playing professional matches so early needs physical and emotional support. Arsenal have recent experience of integrating young players such as Saka, Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly, but each athlete has his own process.

His first professional contract will be signed when he turns 17 on 31 December, after he agreed a pre-contract with Arsenal in January. The decision to stay at the club is important for the continuity of a development that has been closely monitored since the youth ranks.

The path to the senior England team is also open, but does not need to be taken immediately. Bellingham, who lost the Under-21 records to Dowman, played only four matches at that level before being promoted to the senior team.

For now, the best way to assess Dowman is to look at what he can already do, without turning every record into a career prediction. The rest depends on development, opportunities and careful management.
