#1887. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#1886. Michael Carrick speaks out on his Man United sacking for the first time - and admits 'we've not had the results lately' - as Mauricio Pochettino replaces him

Published: 07:48 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 08:08 EST, 13 November 2026

Michael Carrick has released his first public statement on his Manchester United sacking, calling the job an 'immense privilege' in a classy 411-word tribute to the club's supporters.

The statement, released a little over 24 hours after his dismissal was confirmed, read: 'Dear United Fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

'There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

'With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else.

'Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

'It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

Michael Carrick has broken his silence on his sacking by Manchester United

'We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

'I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

'That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

'A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

'To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

'And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead.

'I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

'I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on. Michael.'

The statement follows his former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that Carrick had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of the United legend.

Carrick was left in the lurch by the club's hierarchy - but continued to attend training on Tuesday and Wednesday – amid widespread reports that he would imminently be relieved of his duties.

The classy statement follows Carrick former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that he had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of his dismissal

Neville told Sky Sports News: 'In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

'It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued.

'The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.

'I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all.'

Less than an hour prior to Carrick's statement United confirmed his replacement, Pochettino, will take the reins after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the US’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday.

His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week due to his remaining contracted to US Soccer.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’

#1885. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils to consider legal action over JJ Gabriel's Real Madrid move?

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 12:44

Manchester United are reportedly prepared to take legal action over JJ Gabriel's proposed move to Real Madrid if they uncover any evidence of inducement.

Gabriel revealed back in September that he wanted to leave Old Trafford after failing to break into the senior team.

Although he remains registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving elsewhere in the European Union once he turns 16.

A host of clubs were interested in signing the youngster, but it now appears that he is set to join Real Madrid.

Gabriel posted a farewell message to Man Utd supporters, thanking the club for their role in his development, but the Red Devils are understood to be angered by his decision.

According to the Manchester Evening News, the Red Devils were disappointed that the video was posted without any prior contact from Gabriel's representatives.

Man Utd have reportedly made several attempts to check on the teenager's welfare since he requested to leave, but have been unable to establish contact with his family.

Meanwhile, agency Epic Sports has become Gabriel's new representative, with the club believing that the youngster has been poorly advised by his father throughout the process.

The Red Devils are prepared to explore every available legal avenue should evidence of inducement from Madrid emerge, given the strict regulations surrounding the recruitment of players under the age of 18.

The youngster only turned 16 on October 6, and there was little reason to believe that his pathway to the first team would have been blocked at Old Trafford.

Critics may argue that Man Utd could have handled his development better, perhaps following Barcelona's approach with Lamine Yamal, although such success stories are relatively rare.

What appears particularly surprising is Gabriel's decision to join Real Madrid, where he would face competition from the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in the senior side.

Man Utd can hardly be held solely responsible for his decision, but the way this saga has unfolded could raise questions about the club's ability to retain and nurture its most promising young talents.

#1884. ‘I’m very healthy’ – Kompany returning to the dugout when Bayern host Koln

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany will return to the touchline for the first time since October, when Bayern Munich host Koln in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Kompany has been recuperating after being taken to hospital following a collapse at the club’s training ground last month. He was subsequently diagnosed with meningeal irritation.

In his absence, Bayern have continued their strong start to the season and sit top of the table after nine games with 21 points (W6 D3).

They went into the international break on the back of a 2-1 win over Mainz, and they are looking to move clear of Borussia Dortmund before the rest of the weekend's action.

"It was very intense," he said. "At the time, it was a new experience.

"Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away from the club and the doctors. I'm very grateful.

"You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process; all the tests were positive.

"I have to say, I'm very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

"Now I feel very good again, and I'm happy to be back with the team."

All smiles ahead of tomorrow! https://t.co/hDRW2I2MSx

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 19, 2026

While Bayern are enjoying an unbeaten start to the season, Koln are sat down in 15th, having accumulated just nine points so far.

They are winless in their last four matches (D2 L2), but no matter what, Kompany is relishing the contest.

"There's one person at Bayern who is really motivated for this game against Koln. I've been waiting for four weeks," he said.

"It wasn't difficult to get myself in the right frame of mind. I've had plenty of time. Motivation is always high for every match, and it certainly is for this one.

"I hope I can convey that to the team. They're just back from international duty. It's a Friday game, so anything can happen. If the players can sense my motivation, we'll have a good foundation for the match."

Kane has failed to score in his last four matches in all competitions, his joint-longest goal drought for Bayern.

However, he has already provided eight assists in the Bundesliga this season, a new record for a player after nine matchdays since Opta began recording this data in 2004-05 and already equalling his personal record for a single Bundesliga season (also 2023-24 and 2024-25).

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 19, 2026

El Mala recently scored his 16th Bundesliga goal for Koln; only Dieter Muller (32) and Lukas Podolski (22) scored more Bundesliga goals for the club before their 21st birthday.

Among all U21 players in Europe's big-five leagues since the start of last season, only Barcelona's Lamine Yamal (26) has scored more goals than El Mala (16).

Bayern have not lost any of their last 22 Bundesliga matches against Koln (W20 D2) since a 2-3 away defeat in February 2011.

Among current Bundesliga teams, Bayern only have a longer unbeaten run against Schalke (24 matches).

Indeed, Bayern are the only team from Europe's big-five leagues to remain unbeaten in all competitions this season (W11 D5). They have lost only one of their last 41 matches in all competitions across two seasons, a 4-5 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-final first leg in late April.

Of all teams to have played continuously in the Bundesliga since the start of last season, Koln have won the fewest points over the last 34 matchdays (27), while Bayern have won the most (83).

Over the last eight matchdays, only Borussia Monchengladbach have won fewer points (four) than Koln (six).

Koln are also winless in their last 17 Bundesliga away games (D7 L10), the longest current run of any team in the competition and equalling their negative club record set in 2003-04.

#1883. PM: Hojbjerg still an option for Milan – January move possible thanks to €15m price tag

AC Milan are reportedly interested in making a move for Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg when the January mercato opens, it seems.

There have been suggestions about a move for Hojbjerg for some time, and Milan could attempt a move in January, especially if Christian Comotto departs on loan. The Dane, according to PianetaMilan, is still an option for January if another midfielder is to arrive.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Of course, Luka Modric’s likely retirement at the end of the season will give the Rossoneri time to think about his replacement, or even replacements, and Hojbjerg could be a new tool for Ruben Amorim.

His contract with Marseille runs until the summer of 2028, so his value is only dropping, especially as he gets older. So, a bid of €15 million could be enough to land him.

#1882. Chelsea news: Manager merry-go-round exposes flaws of BlueCo model at Strasbourg

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:46

Has Strasbourg become a prisoner of BlueCo’s strategy? The departure of Hugo Oliveira, replaced by Vitor Matos after only a few months in the dugout, has reignited questions over the management of the Alsatian club.

Only 13th in Ligue 1 with 10 points after 10 games, Strasbourg are going through a very difficult start to the season. But beyond the results, it is above all the absence of continuity that stands out. Since January, four managers have followed one another in the Strasbourg dugout. Such instability is hard to reconcile with building a genuine sporting project.

Liam Rosenior’s departure for Chelsea last January had already given a glimpse of the limits of the model. The Englishman, now at Paris FC, had established a playing identity and allowed Strasbourg to rediscover a certain ambition, before being called up to the flagship club of the BlueCo galaxy.

Gary O’Neil succeeded him, before joining Ipswich Town a few months later. Hugo Oliveira, who arrived this summer, ultimately lasted only four months. Vitor Matos is now expected to succeed him.

This succession of changes raises an obvious question: how do you build a team when its manager changes so regularly?

Each coach arrives with his own principles, tactical preferences and recruitment needs. Rosenior’s high press, O’Neil’s orientations and Oliveira’s intentions have not allowed lasting continuity to be established. Strasbourg’s players constantly have to adapt, while collective automatisms are called into question.

The transfer window does not help matters. Strasbourg had a particularly busy summer, with a multitude of movements, including several players from the Chelsea ecosystem.

The club sometimes looks more like a piece in a vast player circulation system than one building its squad around clearly identified needs. Strasbourg’s sporting logic therefore seems regularly to come second to that of BlueCo.

It would be unfair, though, to deny the benefits of this policy: Strasbourg have rediscovered a European dimension and reached the semi-finals of the Conference League in spring 2026. The club also has a young squad with resale value, and has the resources to attract promising talent.

But what is the point of developing players if the best of them are liable to leave as soon as an opportunity arises within the group? What is the point of investing in a manager if he can be replaced so quickly?

Rosenior’s departures and the player movements between Strasbourg and Chelsea illustrate this difficulty in preserving a trajectory of the club’s own.

BlueCo has found in Alsace a tremendous breeding ground for its young talents. But Strasbourg cannot be reduced to a development centre at the service of Chelsea.

The French club’s supporters expect a team to identify with, a readable project and ambitions that do not change with the owner’s needs. By treating Strasbourg as an interchangeable element of its organisation, BlueCo risks weakening exactly what gives the club its value: its identity. Unless it is already too late? Strasbourg would benefit from disengaging from this stifling structure.

#1881. 'I was one day away from falling into a coma': JAKE O'BRIEN, the Premier League's only diabetic player, on his brush with death, managing his condition in the dressing room - and why he was 'never close' to leaving Everton last summer

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026

There are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door. So you can imagine the reaction Jake O’Brien received when he pulled out his mobile just before one half-time team talk.

But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.

O’Brien’s body is unable to create insulin, the hormone that regulates the amount of glucose in your blood.

Loaded on his mobile is an app linked via Bluetooth to a circular device on his arm which gives a reading of his blood sugar levels. It is then that he takes out a needle and injects the necessary insulin dose into his thigh or stomach.

‘There was one guy who didn’t react too well. Mentioning no names! He was saying: "What are you doing on your phone?"' O’Brien recalls. ‘But he soon realised what it was for.’

It can also come as a shock to the uninitiated among his team-mates.

‘One or two are taken aback at first,’ he says. ‘It can be a bit confusing. “What’s he doing?’’ Or maybe those that are a little squeamish, but they soon get used to it. It's only a small needle.'

Everton and Ireland defender Jake O'Brien is the only diabetic footballer in the Premier League

O'Brien (pictured attending an awareness workshop put on by Everton) revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador

O'Brien (pictured with his partner Sophie) says some of his team-mates are 'taken aback' when he injects himself with insulin (Source: Instagram/Obrienjake_)

Tracking blood glucose levels is now an everyday part of O'Brien's life but it is a life that was unwittingly put in jeopardy prior to his diagnosis at 16.

O’Brien was later told he had been just one day away from slipping into a coma when his concerned parents ushered him to the doctors near the family home in Youghal, County Cork, for a check-up.

Their sports-mad son, who had won national titles at boxing and hurling, was tired, losing weight and had an insatiable thirst despite drinking eight to nine litres of water a day. He had lost seven kilograms in just over a week. A blood test revealed his blood sugar was ten times what was considered stable and he was rushed to hospital.

‘I was told I was a day away from a coma,' says O'Brien. 'If I had gone to sleep that night without having gone to the doctor, who knows?’

He went into hospital that night weighing 53kg, or just over eight stone. Two weeks post-diagnosis he was back up to 60kg, and within two years he had put on a whopping 30kg.

'Yeah, 30kg,' laughs O'Brien. 'I know it's not normal. It must have been some grocery bill for Mum, but I was motivated to put on the weight, going to the gym all the time.

‘I was a bit naive about it all,' he deadpans. ‘I never expected to have anything but once I knew what diabetes was, I didn’t wallow in it, I took it as a positive. Everything just clicked for me physically. I just thought, "Right, now I know what’s wrong, I can get on with my life again".

‘It was a pain going in and out of hospital, but I just took it as education and wanted to get my sport back on track.

'My family are... I wouldn't say cold, but matter of fact. Supportive, obviously, but they are all sporty too, so it was just, "Get on with it".'

O'Brien's life in the Premier League would have seemed inconceivable when he fell down to 53kg as a teenager and was hospitalised

He is now an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with

Today, relaxing in the cafe at Everton’s Finch Farm training complex, O’Brien is an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

There’s a Cork-lilt to his softly spoken Irish tone. He’s polite and engaging and it’s clear he revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador, spreading the message that diagnosis doesn’t have to end your dreams.

Such has been his impact, he has even attracted support from fans of the other club in the city.

One, six-year-old Liverpool fan Louis, reached out via Instagram to ask O’Brien how he kept up his glucose levels during a game and whether he suffered any ‘hypos’ - the expression for hypoglycemic episodes, when the blood sugar drops too low and leaves you faint or dizzy.

Louis, whose siblings Paisley and Evie also have Type One diabetes, followed up by challenging O’Brien to a penalty shootout. If the Everton man lost, he faced a forfeit, he would have to shout ‘Up the Reds’ on social media.

‘You play for the wrong team but you're still a Type One hero, and Mum says you're proof that diabetes doesn't stop you from playing at the top level,’ posted Louis.

Touched by the message, O’Brien asked Everton to invite the youngster and his family to training for a kickabout, although ultimately, we are assured they reached a compromise on the penalties forfeit.

‘I’ve struck up a rapport with some kids and groups here and in Ireland,' says O'Brien. 'They often have the same story as mine of not being sure what the future holds.

‘There’s a big misconception about diabetes over what it is and the limitations it brings.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over.’

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel. I may inject four times before a night game and a bit more at half-time'

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over,’ says O'Brien, who also excelled at boxing and hurling as a boy (Source: TikTok/Everton)

The centre back credits boxing for helping discipline with his diet but underlines ‘no food is off limits, it’s just about applying common sense'.

A typical day sees him eat eggs, salmon and dates for breakfast to match his insulin doses to the carbohydrates he’s taking on around 9.30am before training. Afterwards he’ll have a light lunch at 2pm then take something back from the training ground for a light evening meal.

‘I just have to watch carbohydrates. I’ll eat more of them on match day but then work out my insulin ratio to the amount I eat and whether I need to inject more.

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel, I may inject four times before a night game and inject a bit more at half-time. If it’s not quite right you may get a bit heavy-legged or if I get a few cramps I may need a gel. But I've had no dangerous episodes.'

When World Diabetes Day dawns on Saturday, O’Brien will be fully focused on preparing to play for Ireland in Austria in the Nations League.

It will give him a chance to revert to his favoured centre back position having been asked to fill in predominantly at right back under David Moyes.

He acknowledges it's not his preferred role but dismisses rumours that he wanted to leave as a result in the summer.

'There was nothing in that,' O'Brien affirms. ‘I was never close to leaving.

'People know I'm not a natural right back but I'll play wherever I need to, to help the team. We're only a small squad so it’s important everyone chips in.

‘There’s a lot of different right backs. I see Arsenal have centre backs playing at right back so I can take pointers from them but then again, I am 6ft 6in so I’m not the average shape.’

O'Brien insists there was 'nothing in' reports that he wanted to leave Everton last summer to get more minutes at his preferred position of centre back

At least O’Brien has former Everton captain Seamus Coleman on hand for advice.

‘Seamus is a good friend. He still gives me pointers of where to be, positioning wise and seeing the game differently.'

Ireland assistant John O'Shea, a versatile defender himself in his Manchester United days, is another mentor. O’Shea and Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson were at Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch O'Brien play his part in Everton's recent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

'Heimir is a good guy,' says O'Brien. 'Very understanding. It's always a nice change of scenery to link up with Ireland. We've got a difficult couple of games (Austria and Kosovo) but hopefully if we get two wins it’s within reach.'

Indeed, if there's a mantra that personifies O'Brien's outlook on life, no matter what knocks you take, it is: always believe you can still achieve.

'Don’t be afraid and don’t let anything hold you back, that's what I say.'

#1879. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery 'interested' in midfielder with 155 Chelsea appearances

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 12:53

Aston Villa have reportedly identified AC Milan midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek as a potential winter transfer target.

Earlier on Wednesday, Villa announced that one of their current engine-room options had penned a new long-term contract.

Unai Emery is also not short of players for that position, with Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka and Ross Barkley earning regular minutes.

Nevertheless, not helped by the inconsistent performances and individual mistakes of some of those aforementioned players, Villa remain off the pace in the Premier League.

According to Calciomercato, Loftus-Cheek has emerged as a possible option for the turn of the year.

The report alleges that Villa Park is viewed as a 'potential destination' for the former Chelsea midfielder.

Loftus-Cheek contributed 13 goals and 18 assists from his 155 appearances in a Blues shirt, but he has been at San Siro since the summer of 2023.

His stint at AC Milan can be viewed as a relative success, with 13 goals and four assists coming from 109 outings for the Italian giants.

However, the 11-cap England international's contract is due to expire at the end of the season, putting him in a position where he could leave on a free transfer in the summer.

Milan are open to cashing in on the 30-year-old in order to free up transfer funds and space on their wage bill.

Ruben Amorim's side have also won their last two matches against Inter Milan and Genoa, games which Loftus-Cheek missed through injury.

Despite Loftus-Cheek possessing qualities that Emery arguably lacks within his squad, a move to Villa makes little sense for the player.

Villa already have too many options in the number six, eight and 10 positions in Emery's familiar 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-1-1 formations.

Although Tammy Abraham has been linked with an exit from Villa, it seems unlikely that Loftus-Cheek would transition into a backup number nine behind Nicolas Jackson and Brian Madjo at this point of his career.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#1876. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1873. AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:59

The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

With four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

The last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.

One by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX

While waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

#1872. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.
